Fix an integer \(e\ge 0\). Throughout, \(\mathbb P(V)\) parametrizes one-dimensional complex subspaces of the fibres of a vector bundle \(V\), and \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(V)}(1)\) is the dual of the tautological line subbundle. Let
\[
X=\mathbb P_{\mathbb P^1}\bigl(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\oplus\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(e)\bigr),\qquad \pi:X\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1.
\]
Let \(f\) be the divisor class of a fibre of \(\pi\), and let \(S\) be the section defined by the displayed summand \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(e)\). Thus \(S^2=-e\), \(S\cdot f=1\), and \(f^2=0\). Set
\[
H=S+(3e+1)f,\qquad P=4H-f,
\]
\[
E_0=\mathcal O_X(5S-f)\oplus\mathcal O_X\bigl(-S+(12e+5)f\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathcal O_X(D)\) denotes the line bundle associated with a divisor \(D\). Write \(\bar\partial_0\) for the split Dolbeault operator of \(E_0\).

Suppose \((\bar\partial_j)_{j\ge1}\) is a sequence of smooth integrable Dolbeault operators on the underlying smooth complex bundle of \(E_0\). Thus \(\bar\partial_j^2=0\). Assume that \(\bar\partial_j-\bar\partial_0\), viewed as an endomorphism-valued \((0,1)\)-form, tends to zero in every finite \(C^m\) norm, measured using fixed smooth background metrics and connections. Let \(E_j\) denote the resulting holomorphic rank-two bundle.

Assume every \(E_j\) is ample and slope-stable with respect to \(P\). Here ampleness means that \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E_j^*)}(1)\) is ample; a line bundle is ample if some positive tensor power has a complete linear system giving a projective embedding. Slope-stability means that every nonzero coherent rank-one subsheaf \(\mathcal F\subset E_j\) satisfies
\[
c_1(\mathcal F)\cdot P<\frac{c_1(E_j)\cdot P}{2},
\]
where \(c_1\) is the first Chern class and the dot denotes intersection on \(X\).

Define the complex fourfolds
\[
U_j=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X\oplus E_j)\setminus\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X),
\]
where the removed section comes from the first summand. For a complex fourfold \(U\), define \(\kappa(U)\) to be the least positive integer \(q\) for which there exist a smooth function \(\psi:U\to\mathbb R\) and a compact subset \(K\subset U\) such that every sublevel set \(\{\psi\le c\}\), for \(c\in\mathbb R\), is compact and the Levi form of \(\psi\) has at least \(5-q\) strictly positive eigenvalues at every point of \(U\setminus K\). The Levi form is the Hermitian form with matrix \((\partial^2\psi/\partial z_a\partial\bar z_b)\) in local holomorphic coordinates.

Determine \(\displaystyle\lim_{j\to\infty}\kappa(U_j)\).
</problem>

59	## 2. What a \(2\)-convex end would imply

61	Call a function \(N:V\to[0,\infty)\) a **plurisubharmonic fibrewise seminorm** if it is finite and plurisubharmonic on the total space of \(V\), and its restriction to every fibre is a complex seminorm. It is a fibrewise norm if it vanishes only on the zero section.

64	
65	### Lemma 1
66	Let \(E\) be a rank-two holomorphic bundle over a compact complex surface, and put
67	\[
68	U=\mathbb P(\mathcal O\oplus E)\setminus\mathbb P(\mathcal O).

71	
72	### Proof

74	#### (a) The compact graph lines

76	For \(\lambda\in E_x^*\), define the compact projective line

78	C_\lambda

80	\]

83	F(\lambda)=\max_{p\in C_\lambda}\psi(p).

86	\[
87	[\lambda(v):v]
88	\]

90	
91	We claim that \(F\) is plurisubharmonic wherever
92	\[
93	F>\max_K\psi, \tag{2}
94	\]
95	where \(K\) is the compact exceptional set for the Levi condition.
96	
97	Here is the local argument, including the relevant linear algebra. Let \(\phi\) be a smooth upper test function for \(F\) at \(\lambda_0\), and choose a maximizing point \(p_0\in C_{\lambda_0}\). On the universal family of graph lines, let
98	\[
99	p:\mathcal C\longrightarrow E^*,\qquad
100	\mathrm{ev}:\mathcal C\longrightarrow U
101	\]
102	be the parameter projection and evaluation. The function
103	\[
104	\psi\circ\mathrm{ev}-\phi\circ p
105	\]
106	has a local maximum at \((\lambda_0,p_0)\). Therefore
107	\[
108	\mathrm{ev}^*\mathcal L_\psi\leq p^*\mathcal L_\phi. \tag{3}
109	\]
110	
111	Suppose \(\mathcal L_\phi\) were negative on a parameter direction \(\eta\). Let \(t\ne0\) be tangent to the projective-line fibre of \(p\), and choose \(w\) with \(dp(w)=\eta\). On the complex two-plane
112	\[
113	W=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{t,w\},
114	\]
115	the right side of (3) is nonpositive.
116	
117	Evaluation is injective on \(W\). Indeed, if \(at+bw\ne0\) belonged to its kernel, then \(b\ne0\), since evaluation embeds each graph line. But (3) would give
118	\[
119	0\leq |b|^2\mathcal L_\phi(\eta,\eta)<0,
120	\]
121	a contradiction.
122	
123	Thus evaluation maps \(W\) to a complex two-plane on which \(\mathcal L_\psi\) is nonpositive. This is impossible for a Hermitian form with at least three positive eigenvalues in complex dimension four: every complex two-plane intersects its positive subspace nontrivially.
124	
125	Hence every upper test function for \(F\) has nonnegative Levi form. The upper-test characterization of plurisubharmonicity proves the claim.
126	
127	#### (b) Balanced convex sublevel sets
128	
129	Define
130	\[
131	G(\lambda)=\max_{|a|\leq1}F(a\lambda).
132	\]
133	It is continuous, proper, and invariant under multiplication of \(\lambda\) by complex numbers of modulus one. By (2), it is plurisubharmonic wherever its value is sufficiently large: locally there, only branches \(F(a\lambda)\) lying in the plurisubharmonic region can attain the maximum.
134	
135	Choose \(c\) larger than this threshold and larger than all values on the zero section. Set
136	\[
137	D=\{G<c\}\subset E^*.
138	\]
139	Then \(D\) contains the zero section, is relatively compact, and has a plurisubharmonic defining function near its boundary.
140	
141	Its fibres are balanced and convex. Indeed, \(\lambda\in D_x\) means
142	\[
143	\psi([a\lambda(v):v])<c
144	\quad\text{for every }[v]\in\mathbb P(E_x),\ |a|\leq1. \tag{4}
145	\]
146	If \(\lambda,\mu\in D_x\) and \(0\leq s\leq1\), then
147	\[
148	|s\lambda(v)+(1-s)\mu(v)|
149	 \leq\max\{|\lambda(v)|,|\mu(v)|\}.
150	\]
151	For each fixed \(v\), condition (4) includes the whole disc of possible first coordinates. It therefore holds for \(s\lambda+(1-s)\mu\). Balancedness is immediate.
152	
153	Let \(N\) be the fibrewise Minkowski functional of \(D\). The fibres being bounded, balanced, convex neighbourhoods of zero, \(N\) is a fibrewise norm.
154	
155	For clarity, the standard Minkowski-functional argument gives
156	\[
157	\log N\quad\text{plurisubharmonic off the zero section}. \tag{5}
158	\]
159	One can see this directly by the analytic-disc comparison principle. If \(\log N\) failed harmonic comparison on a disc, multiply the fibre coordinate by the exponential of a holomorphic function to arrange that the disc boundary lies strictly in \(D\), while an interior point lies outside \(D\). Starting with a sufficiently small scalar multiple of this disc, increase the scalar to the first contact with \(\partial D\). At that contact, \(G\) is subharmonic along the disc, is at most \(c\), and attains \(c\) at an interior point. Its contact set is therefore open as well as closed, contradicting the strict boundary inclusion.
160	
161	This proves (5). Hence \(N\) is plurisubharmonic off zero. Locally \(N\leq C|\lambda|\), so it extends plurisubharmonically by zero across the zero section. ∎

163	## 3. Compactness of these norms under convergence of Dolbeault operators
164	
165	### Lemma 2
166	Suppose holomorphic structures \(V_j\) on a fixed smooth bundle over a compact complex manifold converge smoothly to \(V_0\). If every \(V_j\) has a plurisubharmonic fibrewise norm, then \(V_0\) has a **nonzero** plurisubharmonic fibrewise seminorm.
167	
168	### Proof
169	Fix a background norm and multiply each norm \(N_j\) by a positive constant so that
170	\[
171	\max_{\substack{x\in X\\|\xi|=1}}N_j(x,\xi)=1. \tag{6}
172	\]
173	
174	Smooth convergence of the Dolbeault operators gives, on sufficiently small fixed coordinate polydiscs, holomorphic frames for \(V_j\) converging smoothly to frames for \(V_0\). This is the local parametric form of holomorphic triviality; it also follows by successively solving the small matrix-valued \(\bar\partial\)-equations in each coordinate.
175	
176	In these frames,
177	\[
178	0\leq N_j(z,\xi)\leq C|\xi|.
179	\]
180	The compactness theorem for locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions gives a subsequence converging in \(L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\). A diagonal extraction over finitely many bundle charts gives local limits.
181	
182	The fibrewise norm laws pass to the limit. More explicitly, the triangle inequality gives the uniform estimate
183	\[
184	|N_j(z,\xi)-N_j(z,\eta)|\leq C|\xi-\eta|.
185	\]
186	Consequently, after extraction, convergence is uniform on compact fibre sets for almost every base point. The limits are seminorms there. Averaging in the base, passing to the limit, and then decreasing the averaging radius to zero extends the seminorm inequalities to every base point. The converging transition matrices ensure that these local limits glue to a plurisubharmonic fibrewise seminorm \(N_0\).
187	
188	Finally, the limit is not zero. Choose unit vectors \((x_j,\xi_j)\) attaining (6), and pass to a convergent subsequence. In one of the converging local trivializations, the plurisubharmonic functions \(N_j\) have value \(1\) at points converging to an interior point. Their submean inequalities give a uniform positive lower bound for their integrals on a fixed small ball. Their \(L^1\)-limit is therefore nonzero. ∎
189	
190	## 4. The split dual admits no such nonzero seminorm
191	
192	We now show
193	\[
194	E_0^*=A^*\oplus B^*
195	\quad\text{has no nonzero plurisubharmonic fibrewise seminorm}. \tag{7}
196	\]
197	
198	We use an elementary observation. If a positive-degree line bundle
199	\(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(d)\), \(d>0\), carries a finite plurisubharmonic fibrewise seminorm, that seminorm is zero. Indeed, for any global holomorphic section \(s\), the function \(N\circ s\) is plurisubharmonic on the compact curve \(\mathbb P^1\), hence constant. The section has a zero, so this constant is zero. Global sections generate the line bundle, proving the observation.
200	
201	First,
202	\[
203	B^*|_f\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(1).
204	\]
205	Thus any seminorm as in (7) vanishes on the \(B^*\)-summand over every fibre, hence everywhere on \(B^*\).
206	
207	For the other summand, consider sections of \(X\to\mathbb P^1\) obtained as graphs
208	\[
209	\mathcal O\longrightarrow\mathcal O\oplus\mathcal O(e),
210	\qquad 1\longmapsto(1,p),
211	\]
212	where \(p\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(e))\). Their images \(C_p\) have class
213	\[
214	C=S+ef.
215	\]
216	They cover \(X\setminus S\), since \(\mathcal O(e)\) is globally generated. Now
217	\[
218	A\cdot C
219	 =(5S-f)\cdot(S+ef)=-1.
220	\]
221	Therefore
222	\[
223	A^*|_{C_p}\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(1),
224	\]
225	and the seminorm vanishes on \(A^*\) over \(X\setminus S\).
226	
227	The triangle inequality makes it zero on all of \(E_0^*\) above \(X\setminus S\). A finite plurisubharmonic function which is zero off an analytic subset is zero everywhere. This proves (7).
228	
229	## 5. The lower bound and the limit
230	
231	Suppose infinitely many \(U_j\) had \(\kappa(U_j)\leq2\). Their defining exhaustions would have at least three positive Levi eigenvalues outside compact sets.
232	
233	Lemma 1 would give plurisubharmonic fibrewise norms on those \(E_j^*\). The dual Dolbeault operators converge smoothly to that of \(E_0^*\), so Lemma 2 would give a nonzero plurisubharmonic fibrewise seminorm on \(E_0^*\). This contradicts (7).
234	
235	Hence
236	\[
237	\kappa(U_j)\geq3
238	\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }j.
239	\]
240	Together with (1), this gives
241	\[
242	\boxed{\kappa(U_j)=3\ \text{eventually},\qquad
243	       \lim_{j\to\infty}\kappa(U_j)=3.}
244	\]
245	
246	Notice that no implication from ampleness to Griffiths-positive curvature was used. Stability supplies the upper bound; the specified degeneration supplies the lower bound.
247
